comparison: Both strongly support the CRISPR-Cas9 methodology and knockdown efficacy (C16-C17, C23-C24, C55, C74, C77). OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor (p<0.0001, 62-71% reduction), while peer reviewers praised the novelty and temporal/anatomic selectivity. Peer review also evaluated baseline characterization claims (C18-C22) that OpenEval assessed separately in R2.

OpenEval R2 addresses baseline EGFP/Cas9 distribution and quantitative characterization (C18-C22, C80-C81), finding it well-supported by figures and literature. Peer review R1 includes these claims but focuses primarily on methodology validation rather than detailed baseline assessment.

Perfect claim overlap (C25-C29). OpenEval finds the heterogeneity analysis and negative results well-supported with appropriate statistics. Peer review rates this UNCERTAIN, identifying it as a 'minor weakness' and suggesting larger sample sizes are needed to determine if gRNA differences are chance or real effects.

Perfect claim overlap (C30-C33). Both strongly support the finding that pulsatile LH secretion is maintained. OpenEval emphasizes statistical methods and lack of correlation with ESR1 knockdown. Peer reviewers explicitly noted this supports the two-compartment model with no criticism.

High overlap on GnRH cFos correlation claims (C34-C38, C57-C58). Both support the findings, though OpenEval notes gRNA-3 did not show significant effects and explains lack of LH correlation. Peer review accepts cFos as reliable proxy but raises concerns about potential gRNA-specific differences in effects.

OpenEval R6 addresses kisspeptin loss observations and mechanistic explanations (C39-C45, C79), finding them supported but noting C44 involves untested developmental inference. Peer review R5 covers broader regrouping analysis including these claims, strongly endorsing the overall approach and conclusions.

Substantial overlap on bilateral loss phenotype and regrouping analysis (C46-C54, C61-C62, C75-C76). Both strongly support the findings. OpenEval notes small sample size (n=4) and post-hoc nature as limitations. Peer reviewers explicitly praised the regrouping strategy and found the convergence of observations 'convincing' despite small numbers.

Perfect claim overlap (C59-C60). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting the preference for cFos lacks direct experimental validation within the study. Peer review rates SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 3 explicitly validating cFos as 'a reliable proxy' given the limitations of single-point LH measurements.

Overlap on unilateral phenotype explanations (C63-C65). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative and untested. Peer review rates SUPPORTED, with no reviewer challenging these interpretations. Peer R7 also includes Wang et al. comparison claims (C66-C68) that OpenEval addresses in R10.

Overlap on Wang et al. comparison and critique (C66-C68, with C12 in OpenEval). Both support these contextual claims. OpenEval notes the critiques are reasonable but represent indirect evidence. Peer reviewers accepted this contextualization without challenge.

Perfect claim overlap (C69-C70). Both strongly support the two-compartment model interpretation. OpenEval notes the study doesn't directly test compartmentalization mechanistically. Peer Reviewer 4 explicitly endorsed this interpretation, stating it 'lends support' to the model.

High overlap on limitations and alternative explanations (C71-C73, C82). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative and untested. Peer review rates SUPPORTED, with reviewers praising transparency and clarity in discussing limitations, viewing these nuanced discussions favorably.

High overlap on background/contextual claims (C1-C15, C56). Both strongly support these literature-based claims. OpenEval notes they establish scientific context with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted this framing with no critical commentary. Peer R10 includes additional citation claims (C79-C85) not in OpenEval R13.
